why: One signature, verified by both ends of the update path: the release check
(scripts/minisign.mjs, checked by scripts/minisign.test.mjs) and the verifier
the app itself calls (minisign-verify through tauri-plugin-updater, checked by
src-tauri/src/update_signature.rs). A second implementation is only worth
having if it agrees with the first.
Produced with the real tools over a 26-byte payload, so nothing here is
guessed: `npx tauri signer generate` and `npx tauri signer sign` with two
throwaway keys. The project's own signing key is not involved, and a
signature over a known payload gives nothing away. `publicKey` is the key as
tauri.conf.json stores it (base64 of the minisign text), `signature` is a
.sig file's whole contents, and `bundlerComment` was read off a bundle that
`tauri build` signed, which is where the `version:` field comes from.

keys.what: the key the fixture was signed with
a second, unrelated key over the same payload
